<thought>To disconnect the amide bond formed in the target, the retrosynthetic step breaks the C–N bond of the amide, yielding the corresponding carboxylic acid and the amine that supplied the nitrogen. The rest of the molecule (the tolyl‑sulfonyl‑phenyl scaffold) remains unchanged. Thus the two precursors are: (1) the same scaffold bearing a carboxylic acid instead of the amide, and (2) an aniline that provides the nitrogen. The SMILES for these precursors are:
- Acid precursor: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1
- Amine precursor: Nc1ccccc1

These constitute the only viable combination for this transformation.
